profile.reading:
1623 Farnam Street occupies a nine-story, roughly 75,000-square-foot building in downtown Omaha that has operated for more than a decade as one of the Midwest's principal carrier-neutral interconnection hubs rather than as a conventional single-tenant enterprise data center. The facility began as Nebraska Data Centers (NDC), and on November 5, 2018, News-Press & Gazette Company (NPG), a privately held media company based in St. Joseph, Missouri, owned by the Bradley family and best known for newspaper, radio, and television properties across the western United States, acquired NDC and reorganized it as 1623 Farnam, LLC. At acquisition, NPG committed to more than $30 million in capital improvements over the following five years, with the prior NDC leadership, including president Todd Cushing, staying on to run the facility.

That capital commitment has been visible in a steady sequence of expansions: a roughly $10 million buildout in 2019, additional floors brought into service in 2021, and a further expansion completed in June 2025 that added 1.5 megawatts of IT capacity and space for 280 racks across the building's final two data halls, bringing the facility's total capacity to approximately 8 megawatts. In January 2026 the company announced it would add a second Omaha facility to its interconnection campus, extending the carrier-neutral model beyond the original Farnam Street building.

The building's draw for network operators is its interconnection density rather than raw power capacity: 1623 Farnam markets itself as hosting more than 60 network, cloud, content, and wireless carriers, including, by its own account, seven of the world's thirteen largest IP-transit providers, plus direct cloud on-ramps such as Microsoft Azure ExpressRoute and the Omaha IX peering exchange. For power resilience and cooling, the facility draws on Cordia's downtown Omaha district energy system, which the companies describe as providing continuous thermal energy and backup power capability during grid disruptions, an arrangement distinct from the on-site generator plants many suburban data centers rely on instead.

Because the building sits near the geographic middle of the continental United States with access to multiple long-haul fiber routes, 1623 Farnam positions itself as a low-latency hub for coast-to-coast traffic and, more recently, as infrastructure for AI workloads, wireless backhaul, and edge computing. What is not publicly disclosed is a detailed tenant roster, lease terms, or a breakdown of how much of the building's capacity is currently occupied versus available - NPG and 1623 Farnam LLC have published capacity and investment figures at each expansion milestone but have not released standing occupancy or financial data for the facility as a whole.

profile.ownership_note: IMPORTANT: the registry operator name is News-Press & Gazette Company (NPG), a privately held media company (broadcast TV, newspapers, manufacturing) established 1951 and run by the Bradley family. reading: The operator recorded in this registry as News-Press & Gazette Company refers to a Bradley family media and investment enterprise whose Omaha, Nebraska data center at 1623 Farnam traces a somewhat complex ownership path. News-Press & Gazette Company, a privately held firm founded in 1951 spanning broadcast television, newspapers, and manufacturing, acquired what was then known as Nebraska Data Centers in 2018 through a new entity called 1623 Farnam LLC, with MVP Capital serving as financial advisor and existing facility president Todd Cushing remaining in place. The new ownership pledged approximately 30 million dollars in capital improvements over five years to develop the site into a carrier-neutral interconnection hub, which today hosts more than 40 network, content, cloud, and IT service providers. Subsequent to that acquisition, the Bradley family sold the majority of NPG's traditional media assets and organized their ongoing investments, including this facility, under a separate vehicle called BERKS Group, so current ownership is best understood as the same family under a different corporate umbrella rather than a change in ultimate control. In February 2025, Fortune reported, based on a footnote in a contract between Trump Media & Technology Group and vendor WorldConnect Technologies, that this Omaha facility hosts a Truth Social data center that became operational around August 2024, noting that Trump Media typically redacts such facility references from its own SEC filings and that Fortune's finding came from the WorldConnect contract rather than direct company disclosure. This registry records that reporting as a well-sourced factual detail without further characterization.
